title: Publication metadata must not chase its own head
summary: Checkpoint evidence should use stable parent, content and verification references rather than repeatedly rewriting the hash of the commit that contains the evidence.
preconditions: A checkpoint contains Git identity and publication evidence.
The containing commit hash cannot be known before commit creation.
procedure: Record the parent baseline before work.
Record content and station commits after they exist.
Use a stable containing-commit or post-fetch verification phrase inside self-recording evidence.
Verify the final hash externally after publication.
decision_rules: Do not create an infinite documentation-only hash chase.
Separate content identity from publication verification.
stop_conditions: Stop publication if a self-reference is unstable, remote state diverges or the evidence cannot identify its source commits.
validation: Macro 02.2 publication repairs and the Macro 03 checkpoint strategy use stable references.

Macro 01.1 provides a second roadmap occurrence: validation basis, documentary closeout and post-fetch publication are separated without chasing the containing hash; future transition to VALIDATED remains a separate review decision.
failure_modes: Repeatedly committing only to replace a hash generated by the previous evidence commit.
Treating a self-recording placeholder as a verified remote hash.
recovery: Preserve the last green checkpoint, replace unstable self-reference with a stable role reference and verify after push.

evidence_refs.claim: Macro 02.2 required publication-evidence repairs and stabilized references.
Publication is verified as a remote restore point.
Macro 01.1 separates validation basis, documentary closeout and post-fetch verification without a self-referential containing hash.

confidence.rationale: Observed and explicitly applied across two independent roadmap publication occurrences; lifecycle status remains CANDIDATE pending a future authorized review.

notes: The documentary closeout records the semantic role of the final commit without treating a planned or self-referential hash as publication evidence.
